identity_bindings.input_title: Clustered Interval Calibration And Synthetic Segmentation Robustness

rubric.instructions: Review the rendered pixels from one normal research-presentations production invocation. Check that each page contains source-specific content from the supplied engineering bundle rather than placeholders; exact CUHK Beamer identity is visible; the main scientific object is prominent and projection-readable; math, native plots, and medical images are semantically correct where present; no internal RRL/GSC/SRC, QA, provenance, workflow, repo path, run ID, or implementation language leaks into audience-facing slides; repeated generic cards or one-template pages are rejected; and the deck reads as one coherent research update rather than disconnected benchmark pages. For multi-workstream bundles, confirm that each workstream stays internally continuous and that any independent workstream transition is visible without inventing a causal relation. Separately review the deck_contact_sheet item as a deck-level rhythm object: adjacent-page density jumps, repeated composition face, overfull or empty pages, redundant summary filler, result -> failure -> next-experiment rhythm, workstream transition balance, and title/object/formula/image alternation must meet a mature doctoral group-meeting or strong conference-talk bar. The top-level package PASS is not enough; provide item-level judgement and observations for deck_contact_sheet. Do not infer visual quality from filenames or hashes.
source_contracts: The engineering regression bundle is public-safe and explicitly excluded from Stage 5 holdouts.
Stage 2 gold/reference pixels are used only for compatible composition selection.
The deck-quality loop may repair at most once and must fail closed/no-winner for unsafe findings or unresolved blockers.

observations: CUHK crest and the purple institutional navigation band are visible.
The clustered-outcome equation, ICC definition, and component/interpretation panel are specific scientific content rather than placeholder copy.
The central formula is large and projection-readable; no workflow, repository, run, or implementation-language text is visible.
item_reviews.summary: Clear model-introduction slide with a prominent, semantically coherent statistical object.

observations: The slide presents three distinct coverage-by-ICC panels for G=8, G=20, and G=50, with a labeled method key and nominal-coverage reference line.
The plotted trend supports the stated conclusion that cluster-robust intervals recover toward nominal coverage as clusters increase.
Chart, data-source note, and interpretation text are visually consistent and contain no audience-facing process or provenance leakage.
item_reviews.summary: Source-specific quantitative result is readable and tied directly to its conclusion.

observations: The slide uses a left-to-right experimental narrative from DGP knobs through clustered samples and interval procedures to coverage diagnostics.
Specific factors—centers, ICC, balance/imbalance, naive iid versus cluster-robust intervals, coverage, width, and bias—make the design concrete.
Arrows and repeated clustered-sample schematics communicate ordering without hidden implementation details.
item_reviews.summary: Coherent experiment-design explanation with a visibly meaningful process diagram.

observations: The grouped bar chart visibly isolates the small-G failure regime across ICC values and labels the 0.95 target.
Error bars, method colors, numerical labels, and the annotated below-nominal robust result support the negative-result claim.
The adjacent prose explains the consequence and next test; it does not expose internal QA or workflow material.
item_reviews.summary: A scientifically legible failure-result slide with the failure evidence and interpretation kept adjacent.

observations: The slide visibly continues from the stated small-G, high-ICC failure evidence into sampling choices, comparator arms, and a go/no-go decision.
DPP, random-batch, and Mondrian alternatives, plus CR2 and wild-cluster-bootstrap comparators, give the proposed experiment source-specific substance.
The directional flow makes this a next-step plan rather than a disconnected generic summary.
item_reviews.summary: Clear result-to-next-experiment transition with concrete manipulations and decision criteria.

observations: The separate workstream is explicitly labeled “Segmentation robustness: independent visual failure analysis,” avoiding an invented causal connection to the interval-calibration workstream.
Input, GT, prediction, error, and same-case ROI crops visibly depict one medical-image case with spatially corresponding regions.
The TP/FP/FN overlay legend and highlighted ROI make the image-comparison semantics interpretable; no internal provenance or implementation text is visible.
item_reviews.summary: Strong same-case medical-image comparison and an explicit, appropriately independent workstream transition.

observations: The contact sheet shows a coherent sequence: title, model, quantitative result, experimental design, failure result, next experiment, then an explicitly independent segmentation analysis.
Adjacent pages vary among formula-led, multi-panel plot, process diagram, bar chart, decision flow, and image-comparison compositions; there is no run of repeated generic-card pages.
The result → failure → next-experiment rhythm is clearly visible across pages 3, 5, and 6.
The model page has substantial open space and the early plot is comparatively compact, but the sequence remains balanced by denser explanatory and image-led pages later.
The segmentation page provides a visually distinct closing workstream while retaining the same CUHK identity and restrained visual system.
item_reviews.summary: Mature research-update rhythm with clear continuity, meaningful composition changes, and a visible independent-workstream transition.

non_blocking_notes: The statistical-model page is intentionally sparse; reducing some unused upper/middle whitespace or modestly enlarging the interpretation panel could improve density balance.
On the coverage slide, the three-panel chart and its fine labels are smaller than the slide title and surrounding whitespace; modest enlargement would improve long-distance readability.
